clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with a lobulated warty lesion on the lower lip that first appeared during her first pregnancy 7 years prior, spontaneously resolved, then recurred during her second pregnancy 5 years later and progressed. Initial dental examination and biopsy were inconclusive. Definitive histopathologic examination revealed a dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate throughout the superficial dermis with epidermal thickening, elongation of rete ridges, eosinophilic bodies, and lymphocytic exocytosis, without signs of neoplasia or malignancy (E002). Immunohistochemistry confirmed positivity for CD138, kappa, and lambda, indicating a polyclonal plasma cell infiltrate consistent with an inflammatory reaction (E005). No systemic workup for plasma cell dyscrasia was documented. The patient was treated with three consecutive monthly 1ml-doses of intralesional triamcinolone acetonide injections (20mg/ml), resulting in gradual improvement with no recurrence at 6-month follow-up (E006).
